cards.title: One coded failure channel from the kit door to the bridge reply
shared_surfaces: apps/desktop/src/lib/bridge.ts:56 doc comment (desktop context; says the page mints only timeout - stale, one-line follow-up, not in this write set)
acceptance: door: the descriptor useWebMCPTool registers (extracted as a pure toolDescriptorFor(spec, handlerRef)) is executed with {stage:'gone', extra:1} against an enum+closed schema -> its execute REJECTS with a ToolRefusal {reason:'validator_failed', errors:[{path:'stage', code:'enum', message}, {path:'extra', code:'unknown', message}]} listing EVERY mismatch, path-addressed, and the handler never runs

cards.body:
## Summary
The kit's execute door turns every refusal and every handler fault into resolved output text, so the bridge reports them as `ok:true` and every consumer (registry, journey ledger, desktop row) records a failed call as a success. Move the kit onto the coded path the bridge already has: a refusal or fault REJECTS with a typed error, a domain answer RESOLVES.

## Description
`runTool` (door.ts) was built 'never throws' so an agent always reads a sentence. But inject.js reads only resolution vs rejection: resolved text is `{ok:true, output}` (inject.js:133), a rejection is `{ok:false, error, reason?}` (:139). So the kit's `toolError` text, a domain miss like `open_group`'s `{ok:false}` (zoomTools.ts:132) and a real answer are one channel, and the reason vocabulary (validator_failed, timeout) never reaches the surface from a kit tool. Two recorded deviations sit on the same seam: the door has no clock of its own (mcp-tools/server-composition: timeouts are door policy) and it reports only the first mismatch as prose (structured-output). The move: door.ts gains `runToolOutcome` returning `{kind:'ok',text} | {kind:'refused',reason,errors[]} | {kind:'failed',message}` with all path-addressed errors and an own ceiling; `runTool` stays as the text rendering of that outcome (direct callers unchanged); the descriptor useWebMCPTool registers (extracted pure as `toolDescriptorFor`) rejects with a `ToolRefusal` for refused/failed. inject.js forwards `reason` only when it is page-mintable (validator_failed, timeout, cancelled) and an additive `errors` array; protocol.md documents both. A page still cannot claim a gate's reason, and nothing loosens.

## Flow
- agent calls a kit tool with a bad argument -> door refuses -> execute rejects ToolRefusal{validator_failed, errors[]} -> inject.js replies {ok:false, reason:'validator_failed', errors} -> the surface feeds a refusal back (ADR 0041) instead of an ok row
- handler throws -> execute rejects -> {ok:false, error:'tool failed: ...'} -> ledger row is a failure
- handler hangs with no caller signal -> door ceiling -> reason timeout
- handler returns {ok:false, ...} as its domain answer -> unchanged ok:true output

## Expected impact
Closes the class 'a page tool failure is recorded as success' at its source for all four apps' kit tools (every useWebMCPTool registration), carries the refusal vocabulary from the page for the first time, and retires two recorded registry deviations (mcp-tools door.ts:136, structured-output door.ts:29). Could break: a consumer that parsed ok:true output text for '"ok":false' - none found in apps/ or src/ by grep; ledgerbox's direct runTool test is pinned as a guard. Coordination: the journey-stage-src scout (same sub-run) may propose a journey-side read of in-band failures; this card fixes it upstream and the journey side then needs nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a kit tool's refusal or fault reaches the surface as ok:false with a closed-set reason and path-addressed errors; a domain answer stays ok:true
Before: 3 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the three guards)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases, in node --test (demo-kit) and node --test with jsdom (athena-bridge), offline
Result: better
Gate: contract

cards.title: Undo says what it put back: refused, partly undone, or 'undo both'
shared_surfaces: docs/adr/NNNN-an-undo-answers-what-it-put-back.md (amends 0111 decisions 2-3: the toast and the History band report a refused or partial undo truthfully and offer the chain)

examples/hirelane/components/board/history.ts:48 - the History band then labels the row 'undone' and removes its Undo

cards.runner_up: The kit Toast holds an agent burst: N acts toasted within a run coalesce into one 'Athena made N changes' toast with Undo all and a hover/focus-paused clock (needs app call sites to tag agent toasts).
cards.body:
## Summary
The kit's undo contract cannot express 'refused' or 'partly', so hirelane tells a person 'Undone' and marks the row undone when nothing changed, and the one action that would work - undo the later move first - is never offered though the app knows which row blocks. Give applyUndo a return value and give the person the chain.

## Description
`undoActivity(db, id, applyUndo)` treats a returning applyUndo as success: it sets `undone = 1` and logs 'Undid #n'. Apps that need to decline have improvised: hirelane logs 'left the stage alone' and returns, so the kit reports a clean undo over it (the History band shows 'undone', the toast 'Undone: ...'); hirelane hand-logs a second row for a partial slot release; ledgerbox throws a private UndoRefused, and its sent-reminder case is a silent no-op reported as undone. The move (undo-history/execution-emitted-inverse: a reversal returns a value so a composition can short-circuit): applyUndo may return `{refused, blockedBy?}` or `{partial}` (void keeps today's meaning). The kit rolls back a refusal and leaves the row undoable, records a partial as one 'Partly undid' row, and adds `{through:true}`: undo the blocking reversible rows newest-first and then this one in one transaction, all or nothing. ActivityLog renders 'Partly undone' and an 'Undo #7 and this' button from the answer. Hirelane's three branches return verdicts (a later move -> refused with blockedBy; a decision -> refused; booked slots -> partial), its toast offers 'Undo both' through the existing Toast action slot (ADR 0111), and the band stops calling an unchanged act undone.

## Flow
- the agent moves a candidate twice; the person presses Undo on the first move in the History band
- before: toast 'Undone: moved X to screening', row says undone, stage still interview
- after: toast 'Not undone: a later move (to Interview) was made after it' with 'Undo both'; one press puts the candidate back where they started and both rows read undone
- after a decision: 'Not undone: an offer was recorded after it', no button

## Expected impact
The person stops being told an act was reversed when it was not, and a blocked undo becomes one press instead of finding and undoing the later row by hand. The kit contract closes the class for every app on undoActivity; ledgerbox's reminder case becomes a one-line verdict return as a follow-up (its existing backlog item). Could break: an app whose applyUndo returns a value by accident - none do (both return void today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a refused or partial undo is reported as such, and a blocked undo offers the chain that works
Before: 1 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the void guard)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases, node --test over node:sqlite scratch databases (demo-kit, hirelane), offline
Result: better
Gate: none
